headline: Highest risk is medium: shared filesystem and shell-capable AutoGPT can feed Botpress with untrusted content, while Botpress’s package-install ability raises moderate supply-chain and workflow-conflict risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can write to the filesystem and call agent protocol APIs, while Botpress has no documented isolation or provenance controls in its profile. That creates a plausible shared-file or message bridge where AutoGPT output could be treated as instructions by Botpress. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes prompt-like content into a shared file that Botpress reads as instructions
IF Botpress ingests external text from a shared workspace without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable shared file handoff between agents
Add a manual review step before Botpress consumes AutoGPT output
Use read-only mounts for Botpress inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can access the filesystem and make allowlisted network egress, but neither profile shows secrets handled or sensitive data classes. Botpress has no documented filesystem access or egress, so a direct leakage path is not established. The main risk is accidental exposure through a shared workspace, which appears limited and not default from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory containing sensitive files
IF AutoGPT is configured to read those files and forward their contents externally
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory
Use separate OS users for each agent
Mount Botpress inputs read-only
Restrict AutoGPT allowlisted egress to non-sensitive endpoints
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before any outbound transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem and shell execution, and Botpress can install packages. Even without explicit write permissions on Botpress, overlapping mutable system access can conflict if they share an environment or dependency tree. Because Botpress’s write scope is not documented, uncertainty prevents a lower rating.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem or container
IF Botpress package installation mutates dependencies used by AutoGPT
mitigations: Run the agents in separate containers
Pin dependencies and lockfiles
Avoid shared writable directories
Schedule package installs outside AutoGPT runs
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs that Botpress may consume, and Botpress is a customer-support agent that could act on those outputs without a documented verification layer. The profiles do not prove direct automation, but they do show a plausible producer-consumer chain. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Botpress uses AutoGPT output as authoritative input
IF Botpress triggers customer-facing actions from that input without human review
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream actions
Add validation rules for AutoGPT outputs
Log and review all inter-agent handoffs
Limit Botpress to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: implement schema validation on AutoGPT outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile shows regulated data classes, residency constraints, or certification mismatches. AutoGPT touches no declared sensitive data and Botpress likewise lists no data classes or compliance obligations. With no documented compliance boundary in either profile, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to include regulated data classes
IF a residency or retention policy is later attached to shared data
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Assign explicit retention policies
Review residency requirements before deployment
Separate regulated workloads from these agents
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
